evidence: First bar 70: the line opens, with no bar line before it, on five repeated d's, which matches the d d d d d at the end of edition bar 70. A bar line follows, then the low d 32nd group, the high g groups, the e group and the high a groups of bar 71. Last bar 72: after the next bar line come the repeated-d 32nd groups of bar 72. The line ends with a custos squiggle rather than new music, so it finishes in bar 72.

The line opens with four groups of repeated 32nd notes (written-out tremolo) followed by a bar line. This matches the end of bar 85's run of 32nds, the first part of which sits on the previous line. After that bar line comes a written-out 32nd group, then tremolo chords, matching bars 86–87. A bar line marked 'f' after the 'cresc.' then starts the tremolo double-stops of bar 88. The line ends partway through bar 88, presumably still within its tremolo chords.

Each four-note group of 32nds is one eighth note written out. Bar 'a' therefore holds only two beats of repeated notes at the G level, so it is the second half of bar 87, continued from the previous line. Bar 'b' plus the first group of the bottom row (the same overlapping group) gives the lower repeated notes, then a quarter and a quarter rest, which is bar 88. Bar 'c' (eighth rest, a slurred eighth pair, rests, a slurred eighth pair, rest, with pp) is bar 89. Bar 'd', with a similar pattern a step higher, is bar 90 and ends the line.

First bar: bar a has the slurred, piano quarter-note descent F–E–D followed by a quarter rest, which matches bar 60. Bars b through g then match bars 61–66 in order. Bar 61 is the forte dotted figure C, A, C, B, G, A. Bar 62 is the piano A–G–A. Bar 63 has eighth notes separated by rests, including G#. Bar 64 is the G eighths with rests, then four E eighths, marked 'cresc a poco'. Bar 65 is the forte written-out sixteenths. Bar 66 is the sixteenths followed by an A eighth and rests. Last bar: bar h is piano, with a rest followed by the repeated sixteenths, then a slurred figure with trills, which matches bar 67. The line ends at a bar line after it.

The line opens with four repeated dotted sixteenths followed by the trill figure, which is bar 67 (♯d repeated). Space 'a' also holds the descending sixteenths and the closing eighth and rests of bar 68, where the bar line was missed. Bar 69 repeats the ♯ repeated-note figure, and bar 70 has the trill run falling to low E. The written-out low-E sixteenth patterns are bars 71–73, with bar 72's abbreviated half notes written out as sixteenths under 'cresc.'. The line ends with the low E eighth pairs beginning bar 74.

The line opens, straight after the clef and key signature, with two ascending groups of eight 32nds with no bar line before them. These match the second half of bar 35, so the line picks up mid-bar. Next comes an ascending 32nd run, then high 16ths and a chord (bar 36). The double-stop chords and dotted figures that follow are bar 37. The two segments of eighths with grace notes are bars 38 and 39. The line ends with the 16th-note figures carrying chordal stems, which is bar 40.

The line opens with rising beamed 32nd-note groups and then sixteenths, which matches bar 40. Segment b has a grace note, sixteenths, eighths and a dotted figure with a trill, which matches bar 41. Segments c and the continuation into the second row are grace-note figures with naturals and slurs, plus a crescendo marking; these match bars 42 and 43. Segment d is the run of 32nd-note groups, which matches bar 44. The line ends in e with a grace note and the first sixteenth/eighth notes of bar 45.

First bar 43: segment 'a', after the clef and the three-sharp key signature, holds slurred sixteenths on e/g with a rest, matching bar 43. Bar 44 follows as the long run of 32nd-note groups. Last bar 49: the line ends with the rest-plus-sixteenth figures of bars 48–49, and the final quarter notes of bar 50 do not appear. Matching was hard because the copy is dense and several bar marks are misplaced, so this end point is the least certain.

The line opens with two quarter notes before the first bar line; these are the end of bar 49. Next comes the G♯ quarter, the G G eighths and the dotted-rhythm figure of bar 50. The ornamented figures in the middle stretch are bars 51–52. They are followed by four bars of sixteenth-note figures, each with two trilled groups, matching bars 53–56. The line breaks off partway through the last of these, bar 56, before the lower-register trill passage of bar 57.

The line opens after the clef and key signature with a short fragment: low eighths and a beamed figure marked 'p.'. This matches the closing Db/F eighths of bar 12, so the line begins partway through that bar. Next comes a bar of repeated eighths with a trill on a dotted note, which is bar 13. Then C, low C, C and a 32nd-note run with F#, which is bar 14. In the second half, D, low D, D and then eighths is bar 15, and slurred eighths ending with 32nds and 'poco f.' is bar 16. The line ends with a dotted C, low C, a trilled B and a low half note, which is bar 17, closed by the final bar line.

The line opens, after the clef and key signature, with a dotted quarter plus eighth (marked cresc.) before the first bar line. This is the tail of bar 38 (g#. b), so the line starts partway through bar 38. Then follow bar 39 (slurred eighth pairs), bar 40 (trilled dotted quarter, eighth, two quarters, f), bar 41 (dotted quarter, eighth, quarter, two eighths) and the broken-chord eighth bars 42–44. Bar 45 is the pp quarters. The line ends with the bar of a low quarter, then eighths with d#, followed by a final bar line, which is bar 46.

First bar: the line opens after the clef and key signature with a low half-note chord, then a quarter and a dotted-eighth/sixteenth pair. That is bar 86. The triplet run with the C# that follows is bar 87, which confirms it. The program missed the bar line between 87 and 88. Bar 88 is the half-note chord, then an eighth marked pp and the trilled figure. The trill-figure bars follow as 89, 90 and 91. Last bar: the final segment holds only the opening eighths and rests of bar 92 (a staccato eighth, rest, eighth, rest), so the line ends partway through bar 92.

First bar 16: after the clef the line opens with an eighth note and rests, then a sharped low note (D#) beginning a group of four 32nds. That matches the end of bar 16 (F eighth, rests, D# 32nds). Last bar 18: after the bar line come 32nd groups on E, E, G and A#. A natural sign then precedes four A groups, which are the written-out A tremolos, so this is bar 17. After the next bar line come four repeated-note groups, the written-out tremolos of bar 18 (G, G, D#, D). The line then ends with a custos.

First bar: the line opens, after the clef and key signature, with a low four-note 32nd group before the 'f'. This matches the D♯–D–D–D 32nd pickup at the end of bar 16, so the line starts in bar 16 and bar 17's repeated E's begin under the 'f'. Last bar: the bottom row has the ♯ and ♮ A groups with 'p' (bar 19's A♯–A–A–A and A♮), then a real bar line. After it come two groups of staccato G–A–F♯-type 16ths, matching the start of bar 20, followed only by the custos, so the line ends partway through bar 20.

The line has only repeated G# notes in small groups, matching the measured tremolo on G#. Before the first real bar line there are about 8 groups (one group is shared by the two halves). That is one full bar of 4 tremolo quarters, i.e. bar 32, and there are no opening rests, so it is not bar 31. After the bar line (marked f) another 8 groups end at the closing bar line, giving bar 33. Bar 34's D/E double stops do not appear.

First bar: the line opens, after the clef and key signature, with a sharp and four written-out tremolo groups on D. These match the D♯/D tremolo quarters that begin bar 34. They are followed by the E–D and E–F♯ figures of bar 34's second half. Section b (G, D♯, E, F♯, G, G with rests) matches bar 35. Last bar: section c (G eighth, rest, then beamed G sixteenths) matches the start of bar 36, which the line ends partway through.

The line opens with a sharp before four groups of repeated 32nds, low in the staff. This matches the written-out E♯ half-note tremolo at the end of bar 50, so the line starts partway through bar 50. After the first bar line come F♯ repeated notes, then a natural for E♮, then a sharp for four groups of D♯. This is bar 51. After the next bar line come two groups of E, then a natural with D♮ groups, which is the start of bar 52. The line breaks off there, partway through bar 52.

The line opens with a full bar of very low beamed 32nd-note groups below the staff, matching the repeated D and B 32nds of bar 50. After the bar line, the written-out tremolo groups around D–F# fill bar 51. The last segment has only about half a bar of 32nd groups, falling from E to D, and ends at a custos. That fits the first half of bar 52 (E, D), with the C# half note carried to the next line. This placement is a best guess, because the dense beaming makes individual pitches hard to read.

The line opens, after clef and key signature, with four groups of 32nd notes and no bar line before them. This matches the second half of bar 56, whose opening half-note tremolo must have ended the previous line. The middle segment holds eight 32nd groups, which is bar 57. The line ends with four 32nd groups, matching the first half of bar 58; its closing eighth note and rests follow on the next line.

The line opens with a lone rest ending the previous bar, which is the rest of bar 84. Next comes a quarter rest, an eighth rest and then pp 32nd-note groups on low C#, matching bar 85. After the next bar line there are about 8 written-out groups of four 32nds, which is bar 86 with its tremolos written out in full. After the bar line marked f, only about four groups of 32nds appear before the line breaks, so the line stops partway through bar 87 (16 32nds followed by a tremolo).

The copyist writes each tremolo quarter-note double stop as a group of four sixteenths. The first barred segment holds only two such groups, which matches the last two tremolo quarters of bar 30; the opening single G sixteenths of bar 30 belong to the previous line. The next two segments each hold four double-stop groups, matching bars 31 and 32. The line ends at the closing bar line after the fourth group of bar 32. The start is the least certain call, because the overlap between the two rows makes the second segment's group count hard to read.

The line opens with four beamed groups of repeated sixteenth double stops, which is one full bar ending at a bar line. It must be bar 33 because the next bar matches bar 34: a quarter double stop, a quarter rest and a half rest. Then come a quarter rest and three repeated quarters (bar 35). The line ends with the sharped whole note F# (bar 36) before the final bar line.

The line opens on sharp-D and natural-D half notes under a slur, which matches bar 113. The bar that follows starts the sixteenth-note groups over the lower notes: four groups for bar 114 and four for bar 115. The line ends after two slashed (abbreviated) groups, partway through bar 116. One extra note-like shape before the first bar line is not matched to the edition.

The first space (a) holds only two tremolo groups over two lower notes, i.e. the second half of bar 116; the line starts with no bar line before it. Space b has four tremolo groups over four lower notes, matching bar 117. Space c has a quarter note, a quarter rest and a half rest over a lower quarter note, matching bar 118. Space d has a quarter rest and three quarter notes (pp), matching bar 119. Space e has the whole note with a tie leading off the line, matching bar 120.

First bar 6: after the clef, the line opens with a high note followed by repeated eighths, a slurred figure with a natural, and descending 32nds. This matches bar 6 (high f#, repeated e's, d natural, descending run). Bar 7 follows, with a trilled dotted figure, rising dotted notes and a second trill. Bar 8 has a high note, repeated slurred notes, naturals and a descending run. Last bar 9: the final segment has the rising 32nd groups with d# and the a#-d turn, then the descending 32nd figures, as in bar 9. It ends at a bar line; the sharp after it starts bar 10 on the next line.

First bar: right after the clef, key signature and handwritten 3/4, the first bar holds only a quarter rest. This matches bar 26, the 3/4 bar with a rest. The next bar, a half note slurred to a quarter, matches bar 27. Last bar: the line closes with a dotted-eighth/sixteenth figure, a quarter and a sharped quarter, which is bar 33 (B. A G D#). Before it come three half-plus-quarter slurred bars (30–32) after the three-quarter bar 29.

The line opens, after the clef and naturals, with a half rest, a low A and an upper chord, which matches bar 98 (bar 97's whole rest is absent). Then come the rest/chord pairs of 99, the sharped chord of 100 and the whole rest of 101. Bars 102–104 repeat the pattern, ending with the sharped chord, rest and half rest of 104 before the final bar line. The trailing sharp is only the start of bar 105's key change.

The line opens with a clef and key signature, then a half rest and a half note marked 'dol.'. That matches bar 22 (rest, then a half note tied over). Bar 23 is the tied half note followed by a sharped half note, slurred on. Bar 24 is two half notes. Bar 25 is the sharp half note followed by the natural half note, and the line ends at the bar line after it. So the line runs from bar 22 to bar 25.

First bar 27: the line opens with an eighth rest, then three slurred beamed eighths descending (B♭–A–G), a single eighth F, an eighth rest and a quarter rest. That is bar 27, not bar 25 (dotted quarter, tie) or bar 26 (chords). Bar 28 follows: a rest, three slurred eighths rising E–F–G, then an eighth F and rests. Last bar 29: a rest, an eighth E, an eighth with a slurred thirty-second-note group, a low quarter D, and a fermata over the closing rest before the double bar. The squiggle after the double bar is only a custos or mark, with no further notes from these bars.

The line opens with a quarter slurred into a dotted-eighth/sixteenth figure and a quarter marked p. That matches bar 6 (C slurred to B., A, G), not bar 2, because bar 6 has that slur and is followed by a tied G–F# plus a G/B chord (bar 7). Bar 8 (chord and rest) comes before the repeat double bar. After it, a lone quarter rest is bar 9. Next come rest-rest-quarter (pp) = bar 10, half-rest = 11, rest-rest-quarter = 12, and a final half note plus rest = bar 13 before the closing bar line.

The line opens, after the clef and key signature, with the rising run of short notes that starts bar 28, so the first bar is 28. The notes marked dolce with a trill, and the slurred, sharpened figure after the next bar line, match bars 30 and 31. A final bar line follows, and a fragment of a beam after it begins bar 32, so the line ends in bar 32.

Bar a (first bar) has four quarter-note chords: a double stop, then a three-note chord reaching a low ledger-line note, then two triple stops. Bar b repeats that pattern, which matches bars 70 and 71. Bar 69 is ruled out because it has only two chords. Bar c (double stop, low ledger note, rest, note) matches bar 72. Bars d–f (rest, low note, rest, note) match bars 73–75. Bar g (last bar: low ledger note, quarter rest, half rest) matches bar 76.

First bar: bar a (rest, two slurred notes, rest, marked p) matches bar 77; bars b and c (rest + slurred 2 notes; rest + 3 notes) are 78 and 79, and d (half note + half rest) is 80. Last bar: e and g have the double-stopped dotted figures of 81 and 83 (g with the flats), f is the half-note double stop plus two quarters of 82, and h (half note + two quarters) ends the line with bar 84.

The line opens after the clef and key signature with four high 32nd-note A's, then low A 32nds, E's, sharpened D's and a natural-D figure. This matches bar 71. Space b is the long run of repeated C# 32nds ending in low G# notes, which is bar 72. Space c starts with low A notes, then C# 32nds, a D-sharp figure, a D-natural figure, and a tie running off the staff. This is bar 73, which the next line finishes.

The line opens after the clef and key signature with rests, then a ♯ eighth slurred into staccato sixteenths, which is the start of bar 67. Next come bar 68 (staccato sixteenths, ♯ eighths, slurred eighths, rests) and bar 69 (rests, ♯ eighth slurred into sixteenths). The line ends after bar 70's staccato sixteenths and its ♯ eighth figure, partway through bar 70.

The line opens with a tie into the beamed figure with a grace note and dotted sixteenths, then the eighths F–A: this is bar 5, whose first F is tied over from bar 4. The line closes with the paired beamed sixteenth groups (E–G alternations) under a slur after the pp, which opens bar 10. In between, the copy shows bar 6 (C–E–C tied eighths), bar 7 (C eighth, low A, G#, A), the repeat sign, then bar 8 (rest and staccato Ds under a slur) and bar 9 (eighths separated by rests).

The line opens with a tie carried over from the previous line into four dotted sixteenths D–F♯–E♯–D, then ♯A–A eighths, a D eighth and rests. That is bar 14, entered without a bar line. The section after the next bar line has rests, a G♯ eighth slurred into C–E♯–D–C sixteenths, then G♯–G eighths, which is bar 15. The last section has C–E♯–D–C sixteenths, G♯–G eighths, then a run of repeated C notes ending at the line-end bar line. That is bar 16, so the line ends there.

Segment a holds a quarter followed by two slurred quarters, matching bar 23. Segment b has a quarter, a dotted-eighth/sixteenth pair, and a trilled quarter, which is bar 24. Segment c is a half note under a fermata, bar 25. After the double bar and repeat dots, the quarter rest that opens segment d is the start of bar 26, so the line ends partway into bar 26.

First bar: after the clef and key signature, the line opens with a half rest followed by the dotted-sixteenth run ending in an eighth note and eighth rest. This matches bar 18, and the next bar repeats it as bar 19. The rest bar marked c stands for bars 20–21 (the edition has two empty bars; the mark above may be a '2' multi-rest). Last bar: bar d has an eighth rest then slurred C♯–B–D eighths twice, which is bar 22. Bar e has an eighth rest then the A–A–D figure with tie and beamed eighths, which is bar 23 and closes the line.

The line opens with sixteenths separated by rests, then the slurred 32nd figures F F D F A / D F A / D F, which is bar 47. The bar line marked at 'a' leads into bar 48 (A, then the D–F♮–B♭ figures) and bar 49 (B♭, then staccato D D D under 'pp'). After the next bar line, the 'Rouf.' repeated D 32nds and the closing ♯E are bar 50, where the line breaks off.

The line opens mid-bar with a low D (the tie from the previous line), followed by four high d sixteenths. That is the end of bar 78; bar 79 follows with d, D D D D and the half-note D marked 'ten'. Bar 80 has the quarter D, the fermata rest and the pocof. sixteenths. Bar 81 has the 32nd-note groups, and the line ends with bar 83, its pairs of eighth C# plus rest, closed by a final bar line.

Opens with the double-stop bar (quarter, dotted-eighth/sixteenth figure, quarter, then single E), followed by the bar with D#, a rest, D and F#, then the D# double-stop bar. Bars 13–15 and 17–19 look the same, but here this run leads straight into a half note plus half rest and then a whole-rest bar (bars 20–21), so the first bar is 17, not 13. The line ends with the tied whole note (22), the half notes with C natural (23), the quarter–half–quarter bar (24) and two slurred half notes (25), closed by a bar line. The slur continues to bar 26 on the next line.

First bar: the line opens with a beamed pair of low eighths, a single eighth, an eighth rest, a dotted quarter D and a high eighth A. That is bar 132's E-D-D, rest, D., A pattern. Last bar: after bar 133's eight eighths and bar 134's two eighths, eighth and two chords, there is bar 135 (chord, rest, two eighth+rest pairs). The line then closes with eighth, rest, quarter rest, two eighth+rest pairs, matching bar 136, before the line-ending bar line.

The line opens after the clef and key signature with a quarter note, a quarter rest and four slurred eighths, which matches bar 53 (quarter C, rest, eighth pairs). The next bar (quarter, rest, eighths) is 54, and the bar with a quarter, rest and two chords is 55. Then come three bars of a half chord plus two quarter chords (56–58). The line ends with a quarter chord followed by an eighth rest and staccato eighths, which is bar 59, closed by a bar line.

The line opens, after clef and key, with the slurred sixteenth group and an eighth plus eighth rest that end bar 45; no bar line comes before them. Next come the alternating sixteenth rests and notes, with the natural f, b and the dotted sixteenth run, which make bar 46. After that are the dotted d sixteenths, the rest/d pattern, the d–g eighths and the eighth double stops of bar 47, closed by the final bar line.

Segment a begins right after the clef and key signature with repeated quarter notes, one with a natural, and ends on an eighth rest; this fits bar 14 (C, C C, C-natural tied to an eighth, eighth rest), though the copyist's rhythm there does not match the edition exactly. Segment b's quarters and beamed eighth pairs match bar 15, and segment c's rest, slurred eighth, quarter, rest and beamed eighths with a sharp match bar 16. Segment d holds the tied-over note, quarters and a closing half note before the repeat double bar, which matches bar 17.

The line opens with an eighth rest, three eighths and a high half note, matching bar 11 (rest, e♯ e e, half note a). The next bar holds repeated A sixteenths, then an eighth and rests, matching bar 12. It closes with rests, a sharped eighth, dotted sixteenths and two eighths whose tie carries over into the next line, matching bar 13.

First bar: the line opens with an eighth rest and beamed eighths on A and no bar line before them, which matches the end of bar 9 (r A A A). Next comes bar 10 (r, A A quarters, A eighth, A A eighths, under 'cresc. a poco a poco'), then bar 11 (eighth rest followed by repeated A eighths, marked f). Last bar: the falling sixteenth groups starting high (ff) followed by eighth notes match bar 12, which ends at the final bar line.

First bar 85: the line opens, after clef and key signature, with a low half-note dyad on ledger lines (A/C), then a rest and a dotted figure, matching bar 85. Bar b is four triplet groups with a sharp, matching bar 86. Bar c is the half note marked with a sharp (C#), then a rest and a dotted figure, matching bar 87. Bar d is two triplet groups, a quarter note, and the trilled A with 32nd notes, matching bar 88. Last bar 89: bar e has the eighth note, eighth rest, and second trill figure, and the line breaks partway through bar 89 at the Bb eighth.

The line opens directly with the repeating figure of a lone low eighth followed by a slurred eighth-note group. This figure fills a, b and c identically and matches bars 73–75. Nothing in the line matches bar 72's opening chord or eighth rest, so the line begins at bar 73. Bar d (quarter note, quarter rest, half rest) is bar 76. e and f are the tied whole notes of bars 77–78, g holds the two halves of bar 79, and h (half note plus half rest) is bar 80. The last bar, i, is marked ff and holds a half note, a high quarter and a low quarter, which is bar 81. Bar 82's chord and repeated quarters are absent.
